CA really should've never shut down its methanol flex-fuel program back in 2000. It's so much easier to produce methanol than ethanol from so many feedstocks (you can make syngas from any fossil fuel and any biomass source). And any vehicle M85 rated would automatically have fuel systems compatible with any other alcohol blend from ethanol up, given methanol is more corrosive and aggressive. (some existing E85 vehicles MIGHT work fine on high methanol blends, but it wouldn't be officially specified for that, so it's up to chance, the M85 program would've made any M85 vehicle E85 compliant, plus any intermediate blend of either, plus propanol or butanol blends ... or 100% butanol fuel ... or E100 for that matter, though that 15% of hydrocarbons is partially there to make flames visible to reduce transparent fire dangers ... the same reason M85 would've been safer to run than M100 fuel in Indy Cars ... before the switch to E100) There's also a whole thing about a fuel economy sweet spot around 25% methanol or 30-35% ethanol (also energy economy sweet spot a bit higher than that), plus those ranges also conveniently being within the range that many (potentially most) non-FFVs with any sort of electronic fuel injection (going back to many 1980s cars, especially the economy 4 cylinders, given Ford and GM implemented EFI on the small engines first, like the 2.3L Ford and 2.5L Tech IV Iron Duke), and can run on such without engine problems, performance issues, or computer faults (and may pass emissions ... and may also allow faulty/worn emissions hardware to pass SMOG tests when E10 won't, often if the EGR valve is bad or going bad, though other factors may be present where alcohol dilution actually lowers emissions to the point of passing;  albeit there some niche cases where around 20% ethanol or E20 makes NOx levels go up, but that's really only an issue if you're running lean and usually it's the CO and HC levels that are high when EGR is bad or catalytic converter is worn, as rich conditions are easier to reach there  ... oh right, also any car with a smog pump with or without EGR as well could have problems there and alcohol in the fuel would lean out rich conditions to be much closer to stiochiometric, plus reduce combustion temperatures similar to EGR ... also raise the octane number and eliminate ping/knock).

That big about 'cheating' emissions tests is more of an aside, but I kind of wonder how many cash for clunkers vehicles would've passed SMOG tests if fueled up with E30 or E35 ... except a lot of those also included early 80s era V8s with the dreaded electronic control carburetors, and if the metering rods go bad in those, you really need a carb rebuild to get that working. (unless they're stuck in rich, in which case the alcohol blend MIGHT be enough to fix things by shifting that into the near-perfect lambda 1.0 stiochiometric point when in cruise: the carb's accelerator pump squirts extra fuel to enrich the mixture when you initially press down on the throttle pedal, but having stoich AFR in steady-state throttle position would get you to low emissions if the catalytic converter is working even if EGR and air injection is messed up). To be fair, it's not really cheating if you run that ethanol blend all the time, which one could usually get away with if you have E85 stations locally.  (running normal pump gas, especially 87 ocane, at that same lamda of 1.0 might cause knock in those same engines at full throttle, which is why EGR dilution and/or rich mixture is used and with rich mixture you need air injection for the cat to work right, but with around E30 to E35, even 87 octane pump gas becomes closer to 93 or 94 octane AKI or likely around 100~101 RON 87~88 MON ... it's not a simple rule of mixtures as ethanol's blending ON is higher than its neat ON, and the lower octane the base stock is, the more impact the alcohol has, and the higher ON the base stock then the less dramatic the blending ON is with ethanol, and methanol is also like this; that also makes such blends unsuitable for the European RON pump rating as they mandate that the MON must be no more than 10 points lower than RON, albeit you could legally rate 100/88 RON/MON as 98 octane fuel in the UK and Europe for that reason)  


Also both methanol and butanol are efficient to produce from syngas (the latter has lower yields, but higher value for gasoline blending due to energy density and low hygroscopicity, so it can be pipelined and now attract too much moisture where methanol and ethanol need to be trucked in and blended straight at the fuel station). Already on agrivoltaic farms livestock are grazing on pasture growing under elevated ground mounted solar arrays.  Plants benefit from the shade of the array and are shielded from heavy rains, hail and sun stress.  
Plants do have a limit on the amount of sunshine they can metabolize known as light saturation point.  Once a plant reaches this maximum rate of photosynthesis the plant starts evaporating water to cool itself.  Agrivoltaics reduce the amount of water evaporation from plants reducing water loss and agricultural water usage.
